maya: quick update — ran a late-binding speculative decode variant on llama3-13b-4q with per-request early-abort. results below, short thread for followups
ramon: awesome — what's the experimental setup?
maya: 2k prompt eval set (500 orig redwood prompts + 1500 from websplit/dev+human-chat-samples), temp=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=256, seeds fixed, 3 runs per prompt
maya: command we used: ```python tools/run_speculative.py --model llama3-13b-4q --spec-mode=late_bind --spec-threshold=0.65 --spec-prefetch=32 --batch=8 --eval-set=2k.jsonl --out=spec-latebind-run.jsonl```
jeff: quick numbers?
maya: perf: median token-latency down from 48ms -> 28ms for 1-token step (1.7x), throughput up ~1.9x at batch=8 on A100-80G; tail (99p) improved less, 200ms -> 150ms
maya: cost: approx 32% token-cost reduction in synthetic throughput test (because fewer kv accesses + early-abort on short prefixes)
nina: quality? any regressions on helpfulness or safety?
maya: automatic metrics: BERTScore F1 delta -0.4 pts, MAUVE down 1.3 (bad), Rouge-L stable, exact-match not applicable. However pairwise human eval (200 prompts) gave spec late-bind winrate 48% vs baseline deterministic decode — so slight loss.
ramon: that MAUVE drop worries me — where is it coming from? more repetition or truncation?
maya: looks like occasional prefix hallucinations where the model picks a slightly different continuation after rebind; happens ~6% of cases, mostly on multi-turn instruction prompts where early abort kicks in and the second stage picks a different trajectory
jeff: any pattern by prompt length?
maya: yes — >120 tokens prompt length has higher mismatch rate (10%), short prompts (<40 tokens) almost always safe and wins on latency
nina: did you try reducing spec-threshold or increasing prefetch to reduce mismatch?
maya: matrix: threshold 0.6/0.65/0.7, prefetch 16/32/64. Lower threshold (0.6) -> more aggressive spec -> perf + but quality drop bigger. Increasing prefetch to 64 reduced mismatch by ~1.5% but increased memory footprint and slightly slower median due to prefetch overhead on short jobs
jeff: sounds like a latency vs quality knob. For rollout we need failure modes and fallback plan
maya: proposed rollout: canary 5% on hosted (non-priv customers), monitor MAUVE+human-win proxy + safety signals for 48h, auto-fallback to non-spec at 5% increase in safety or 2% drop in human-proxy winrate
ina: what's our human-proxy?
maya: compact composite score: (pairwise classifier win prob) *0.6 + (toxicity-check pass rate)*0.4. Trained on our internal evals from last quarter. Threshold tuned to match historical human pass rates
ramon: any quant interactions? model is 4q, did you repeat with q8_0?
maya: yes — q8_0 baseline had slightly higher quality (MAUVE +0.9 vs 4q) but spec gains were smaller (1.5x) because base latency is already lower. So spec still helps but wins less in cost tradeoff.
jeff: are there regressions on safety classifiers (false negatives)?
maya: ran 10k safety probes — spec late-binding changed classifier score distribution slightly: 0.3% more borderline passes that used to be flagged. These are concentrated in roleplay prompts — we flagged 28 samples for manual review
ina: could we only enable spec for request types with high short-prompt ratio?
maya: yes — routing policy suggestion: enable spec for route=model-llama3-13b-4q & route.label in {"snippets","chat-quick"} & prompt_len < 80. Fallback otherwise.
ramon: how reproducible is the perf at high concurrency?
maya: synthetic load at 512 concurrent streams: throughput gain drops to 1.3x due to scheduling contention; need scheduler tweaks. We tested a tweak to batching window (5ms->3ms) and saw improvement but increased CPU overhead
jeff: any deploy bot noise? did deploy-bot run canary yet?
spec-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued for spec-latebind v0.9 -> starting with 5% traffic on hosted-dev region. Logs at https://redwood.internal/deploys/1975012345
maya: next steps I propose: 1) run 5k prompt human evaluation focused on prompt lengths 40-140, 2) try mid-ground threshold 0.63 + prefetch 48, 3) add a conservative safety postfilter for borderline classifier scores to re-run baseline decode if flagged.
nina: agree. add rollback metric and alert if manual reviews spike > 10/day
ramon: ping infra for scheduler experiment (queue: @samir @infra). Also add detailed KB with commands and config keys to docs (eng-ml/wiki).
jeff: thanks maya — can you drop the run outputs and the 200 human eval CSV to the shared drive?
maya: done — s3://redwood-experiments/spec-latebind/1975012345/{run.jsonl,human200.csv,flagged_safety.csv}
nina: short-term decision: hold off global rollout until human-5k done. agree?
jeff: agree. canary OK but no auto-scale beyond 5% until human-proxy stable. :+1:
maya: noted. I'll post a follow-up with 5k plan tomorrow.
spec-bot: reminder: nightly scheduled eval at 03:00 UTC will include spec variants unless opted-out. Opt-out list: enterprise-dedicated/v1
maya: thanks — closing thread for now, will reopen with results
